title: 2026 U.S. House of Representatives election in Arizona's 3rd Congressional District
description: Incumbent Democratic Rep. Yassamin Ansari, first elected in 2024, is seeking a second term representing Arizona's 3rd Congressional District, which covers southern and western Phoenix, downtown Phoenix, and part of Glendale. The district is considered a safely Democratic seat (Cook PVI D+22), and Ansari won the 2024 general election with approximately 71% of the vote. Ansari faces three challengers in the 2026 general election: Republican Nicholas Glenn, Green Party candidate David Redkey, and No Labels candidate Alan Aversa. The primary election is scheduled for July 21, 2026.
polling_note: No publicly available opinion polls were found for this race as of June 2026.

candidates.name: Yassamin Ansari
candidates.summary: Yassamin Ansari is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Arizona's 3rd Congressional District, first elected in 2024. A former Phoenix City Council member and UN climate policy adviser, she is the youngest woman serving in the 119th Congress and serves as Democratic Freshman Class President. Ansari has focused on climate action, reproductive rights, and affordability issues, and in April 2026 introduced articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.

candidates.name: Nicholas N. Glenn
candidates.summary: Nicholas Glenn is a Republican candidate seeking election to Arizona's 3rd Congressional District. Originally from New Jersey, he is a U.S. Navy and Marine Corps veteran who served aboard the USS Kitty Hawk and participated in Operation Desert Shield, Operation Southern Watch, and Operation Restore Hope. After his honorable discharge in 2000, he worked in semiconductor and aerospace manufacturing and currently serves as HOA president for the Baseline Mountain Ranch Community in Phoenix.

candidates.name: David Redkey
candidates.summary: David Redkey is the Green Party candidate for Arizona's 3rd Congressional District. A certified teacher and longtime Phoenix resident, he is an advocate against conservatorship and guardianship fraud and promotes what he calls 'Foundation Economics,' which emphasizes putting people over profits. Redkey is running as a write-in candidate for the Green Party primary and has pledged not to accept corporate PAC money.
